findings.evidence: Slack previews show only the first line, so a buried ask goes unseen.
findings.fix: Replace this widely known fact with a correction the model would otherwise get wrong. One example: it tends to soften a deadline into "when you get a chance", which removes the deadline. The fix keeps the date and softens only the framing.

findings.evidence: Use the diagnosis to choose the next scenario (cooperative, resistant, confused), varying one thing at a time.
findings.fix: Add a rule that maps the result to the next scenario. If the user dropped the ask, repeat the same concern as resistant. If the user resolved it, move to a new concern as confused. If the user over-conceded, switch to cooperative and test whether they hold the ask.

findings.evidence: Cc'ing a manager on feedback reads as escalation even when the tone is soft.
findings.fix: Say what to do about it: "flag the Cc in Biggest risk and suggest sending the feedback 1:1 first". Also add one or two more channel-specific gotchas, for example that a reply-all thread puts a correction in front of the whole team.

findings.evidence: Code, legal or compliance review: decline and say who should own it.
findings.fix: Settle the case of a draft PR comment or code-review reply that the user wants checked for tone. Add: "The wording of a code-review comment is in scope; judging the code itself is not." Without this, the decline rule blocks one of the most common tone-check requests.

Define the three ratings. Strong: no risk-level issue. Needs Work: the ask or tone is off, but sending it as-is would not cause harm. Significant Issues: the Biggest risk would cause a misread ask, an accusation or a lost flag if sent.

findings.evidence: "Pick a concern the counterpart would plausibly have about the user's goal" and "If only optional context is missing (audience seniority, deadline), state your assumption and proceed." Intake, Review and Roleplay occupy 38 of the 54 lines under the six main H2 sections and are predominantly activation of familiar coaching behavior, including output templates, rather than new expert knowledge. The strongest knowledge delta is concentrated in the specific uncertainty, accusation and escalation traps and the repository handoffs.
findings.fix: Preserve the scope routing, required-input fallback, output templates, completion conditions and concrete anti-patterns. Remove the routine optional-context reminder and compress Roleplay steps 1–3 to: "Raise one plausible in-character objection at a time. Privately test whether each reply resolves the concern while preserving the ask; choose the next scenario from that diagnosis, varying one feature." Keep generic coaching narration brief rather than expanding frameworks already supplied by the preloaded skills.

findings.evidence: Keep the author's voice and first person. Lowercase is fine if it fits.
findings.fix: Delete this line. The model already keeps the author's voice when rewriting. Keep only the sensitive-post tone rule on the next line, which the model would not apply without being told.

findings.evidence: choose one primary objective: replies, reposts or dwell. It decides which variant you RECOMMEND
findings.fix: Add a rule for choosing the objective when the user does not state one. For example: a launch or announcement defaults to reposts, a request for feedback or a question defaults to replies, a lesson or story defaults to dwell. Say the chosen default in ANALYSIS. Without this rule, the recommendation in step 5 is arbitrary.

findings.evidence: Write ragebait or exclusionary tribal framing.
findings.fix: Add the reason, as every other NEVER item has one, for example: '...: it brings in hostile replies the author must moderate and cuts the post off from readers outside the in-group'. Also add one or two more Gotchas items that defy assumptions, for example: 'Unicode bold or italic "fancy text" counts as 2 weighted characters per glyph and screen readers read it as noise, so never use it for emphasis.'

findings.evidence: description: Rewrite a tweet idea or draft into three X post variants ... even without the word 'viral'.
findings.fix: description: Rewrite a tweet idea or draft into three X (Twitter) post variants with engagement trade-offs, character counts and a recommendation. Use when the user wants to sharpen a hook, make a post more shareable, turn a launch, lesson or announcement into a tweet, trim a long draft to 280 characters or split it into a thread, even without the word 'viral'. Drafting only; never publishes, schedules or manages an X account.

findings.evidence: Sensitive posts (grief, apology, factual updates): replace (b) and (c) with quieter variants (plain, reflective, minimal), label them so
findings.fix: Change the Output template and step 2 to match the sensitive branch. In the template, write 'VERSION 2 (reply, or quiet variant for sensitive posts)' and do the same for VERSION 3. Also state that for sensitive posts the objective is clarity, not replies, reposts or dwell. As written, the sensitive branch has no objective to choose in step 2, and its output conflicts with the fixed (hook)/(reply)/(repost) labels in the template.

findings.evidence: Count each draft, shorten, recount. If the essential content cannot fit, ask whether to make a thread ... offer a numbered thread.
findings.fix: Give a counting method. Where a shell is available, compute the weighted length with a one-line script (URLs count as 23, characters outside Latin-1 count as 2). Otherwise, count manually and keep a 10-character margin. Also add a thread template to Output, with numbered posts each showing a count, because the thread branch has no format to produce.

findings.evidence: 'Keep the author's voice and first person. Lowercase is fine if it fits.' is standard editing guidance. The prohibition on inventing facts at line 33 also repeats the grounding restriction at line 16. The body mixes useful domain decisions with substantial activation material rather than predominantly adding expert knowledge.
findings.fix: Consolidate factual-grounding requirements into one invariant, trim generic editing reminders, and retain the higher-value supported-contrast, sensitive-post and compression-semantics rules.

findings.evidence: 'choose one primary objective: replies, reposts or dwell. It decides which variant you RECOMMEND' names three objectives, but the following step supplies selection guidance only for discussion versus standalone reach; it never explains when dwell should win or how to evaluate a draft against that objective.
findings.fix: Add a brief dwell-specific decision rule: choose it when the supplied material supports a worthwhile mechanism or contrast that rewards rereading, preserve its complete payoff, and recommend the variant that delivers that payoff without an unresolved curiosity loop.

findings.evidence: 'Skip this limit only if the user says they have an extended-post allowance.' The standard-length and thread branches resolve, but the extended-post branch removes the stated ceiling without establishing the user's actual allowance or a replacement validation limit.
findings.fix: For extended posts, obtain the applicable character ceiling and count, shorten and recount against it. If the ceiling is unspecified and clarification is unavailable, retain the 280-character default rather than treating the allowance as unlimited.
